q: How do I create a financial plan?
a: Calculate your income and expenses, list your assets and liabilities, build emergency savings, set priorities, and review the plan regularly. FREEDOM can keep your records, goals, and debt plan in one place.

q: What are short-term, medium-term, and long-term goals?
a: Short-term goals are usually within a year, such as an emergency fund or clearing a credit card. Medium-term goals take one to five years, such as a vehicle down payment. Long-term goals take longer, such as retirement or a home.

q: How do I prioritise several financial goals?
a: A common order is essential expenses and minimum debt payments, a starter emergency fund, high-interest debt, and then longer-term saving and investing. Your own situation may call for a different order.

q: How often should I review my financial plan?
a: Review spending and debt progress monthly, and goals, insurance, and investments at least once a year. Review sooner after a major change such as a new job or a new loan.

q: What is financial freedom?
a: It usually means having enough savings, investments, and income sources to cover your living costs without depending on one paycheque or on borrowing. The amount needed differs for every person.

q: How much money do I need for financial independence?
a: A common rule of thumb is about 25 times your yearly expenses, but it is only a rough guide. Inflation, taxes, investment returns, and lifestyle can change the figure a lot.

q: What is inflation and why does it matter?
a: Inflation is the general rise in prices over time, so the same money buys less later. Plan goals using future costs, not only today's prices.

q: Do you need my bank password or OTP?
a: No. Never share passwords, OTPs, PINs, or card numbers with FREEDOM or any chatbot. A genuine service will not ask you for them in a chat.

q: Should I share my PAN, Aadhaar, or card number with you?
a: No. FREEDOM does not need them, and you should avoid typing sensitive identity or card details into chats.

q: Where is my FREEDOM data stored?
a: Your records are stored on your own device in the app's local storage. They are not uploaded unless you export a backup or turn on an online feature.

q: Is my data sent to the AI service?
a: Only if you connect an AI service. Your questions are then sent to that provider. Your FREEDOM figures are shared only if you switch that option on.

q: How do I back up my data?
a: Use More, then Backup, to download a JSON file and store it somewhere safe. To restore, choose the file and confirm.

q: What happens to my data if I clear my browser or lose my phone?
a: Local data can be lost. Download regular backups so you can restore your records on a new device.

q: Can FREEDOM move money or pay my bills?
a: No. FREEDOM only records and analyses the information you enter. It cannot access your bank accounts or make payments.

q: What happens if I pay only the minimum due on my credit card?
a: You avoid a late fee, but interest usually continues on the remaining balance and the debt can last a long time. Paying the full statement amount avoids card interest in most cases.

q: Is a personal loan better than carrying credit card debt?
a: Sometimes, if the loan costs less overall once interest, processing fees, and prepayment charges are included. Compare the total cost, not only the EMI.

q: Are buy-now-pay-later and no-cost EMI really free?
a: Not always. Check for processing fees, taxes on fees, late charges, and any price difference compared with paying upfront.

q: Should I borrow for a holiday or a gadget?
a: Borrowing for wants adds interest and a monthly commitment. Saving first usually costs less. If you do borrow, check that the EMI fits comfortably in your budget.

q: How do I know if a loan app is safe?
a: Use lenders regulated in India, read the terms and total cost, and avoid apps that ask for broad phone permissions or pressure you. Never share OTPs.

q: What should I do if I cannot afford my EMIs?
a: Contact your lender early to ask about restructuring or hardship options, cut non-essential spending, and prioritise secured and essential payments. A qualified financial counsellor can help.

q: Why is health insurance important?
a: A single hospital bill can wipe out savings or create debt. Health insurance helps cover major medical costs, subject to the policy's limits and exclusions.

q: What is term insurance?
a: Term insurance pays a sum to your nominee if you pass away during the policy term. It matters most if others depend on your income.

q: Is insurance a good investment?
a: Insurance is mainly protection. Policies that mix insurance and investment can have higher costs, so compare them with separate term cover and investments.

q: Should I buy insurance before investing?
a: Many people secure basic health and life cover first, because a major event can derail all other plans. The right cover depends on your dependants and budget.

q: Do I need to file an income tax return?
a: It depends on your income, sources of income, and the current rules. Check the official income tax website or ask a qualified tax professional.

q: Can FREEDOM calculate my income tax?
a: FREEDOM does not file taxes or give tax advice. Tax rules change, so confirm any figure with the official source or a professional.

q: Which documents should I keep for my loans?
a: Keep the sanction letter, repayment schedule, statements, and payment receipts. They help you check balances and resolve disputes.

q: Are you a financial advisor?
a: No. I give general education and calculations based on the information you enter. For major decisions, consider a qualified professional.

q: Can you guarantee my results?
a: No. Debt dates, savings dates, and investment values are estimates. Interest changes, missed payments, fees, and market movements can change the outcome.

q: Which stock or mutual fund should I buy?
a: I cannot recommend specific products or predict markets. I can explain how they work, their risks, and how they compare with paying down debt.

q: How do I know whether a number is real or an estimate?
a: Figures taken from your saved records are labelled as your entered data. Projections are labelled estimates, and general guidance is labelled as general information.

q: What if my saved data is wrong or out of date?
a: Answers are only as accurate as the records entered. Update balances and values from your latest statements, and I will recalculate.

q: What if I feel overwhelmed by my debt?
a: Many people feel this way, and small steps help. List your debts, talk to your lenders early, and consider a qualified counsellor. FREEDOM can help you track a plan one step at a time.
